# Settings keys

<!-- Generated by `just gen-settings-docs` from the registry in `crates/bisa-core/src/settings.rs`. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every setting is declared once, in `bisa-core`, with the scopes that may hold it. Resolution is
`project → workspace → machine → default`, walking only the scopes a key allows; a write to a scope a
key does not allow is refused. Scopes: **M** machine (`machine.json`, never synced) · **W** workspace
(`settings.json`) · **P** project (`projects/<slug>/settings.json`). See
[ide/13 — Settings](../architecture/ide/13-settings.md).

| Key | Kind | Default | Scopes | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|

| `appearance.accent` | `amber` (Amber) \| `violet` (Violet) \| `teal` (Teal) \| `rose` (Rose) | `"amber"` | M | **Accent** — The accent means your attention. |
| `appearance.density` | `comfortable` (Comfortable) \| `compact` (Compact) | `"comfortable"` | M | **Density** — Rows sized for reading, or for holding more. |
| `appearance.type_scale` | number 0.9–1.5 | `1.0` | M | **Text size** — A multiplier over the base unit: 1 is a 14px body. |
| `appearance.font_ui` | `system` (System) \| `inter` (Inter) \| `atkinson` (Atkinson Hyperlegible) | `"system"` | M | **Interface font** — The face the app reads in; `system` is the OS's own. |
| `appearance.font_mono` | `system` (System) \| `jetbrains` (JetBrains Mono) \| `plex` (IBM Plex Mono) | `"system"` | M | **Code font** — The face the editor, the terminal and every code span use. |
| `appearance.language` | `system` (System) \| `en` (English) | `"system"` | M | **Language** — The language the app speaks. System follows this machine's languages to the first the platform has; English is the one shipped today. Every word — the desktop's, the node's refusals, the CLI's — follows. |

## `browser.*`

| Key | Kind | Default | Scopes | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `browser.enabled` | bool | `true` | M | **Embedded browser** — The browser built into the desktop app — a tab in the Project IDE, and the Browser pane beside any screen. Off, no tab opens, every launcher says so, and agents are told the embedded browser is turned off. |
| `browser.home` | string | `""` | P W | **Home page** — The URL a new tab opens on. Blank opens an empty tab with the address field ready. |
| `browser.remember_tabs` | bool | `true` | M | **Remember tabs** — The tabs you can see, and where each is, are kept across a restart; a tab an agent keeps out of sight never is. Off, the tabs are forgotten when the app closes and none is kept. |
| `browser.agents` | `everyone` (Everyone) \| `assigned` (Assigned) \| `nobody` (Nobody) | `"everyone"` | P W | **Agents may use the browser** — Which agents may drive the embedded browser through the browser tools. Everyone: any agent — the default, since the guard refuses the machine's browser and every catalog agent carries the Embedded Browser skill as its guidance. Assigned: only agents that carry that skill — the platform's own agents always may. Nobody: the tools refuse. |
| `browser.agents.reach` | `anywhere` (Anywhere) \| `local_only` (Local only) | `"anywhere"` | P W | **Where agents may navigate** — Anywhere: any http or https page. Local only: pages served on this machine — localhost, 127.0.0.1 — such as the project's dev server or a folder served from the IDE. |
| `browser.agents.headless` | `unattended` (Unattended) \| `always` (Always) \| `never` (Never) | `"unattended"` | P W | **Agents' tabs out of sight** — When a tab an agent opens is kept out of sight — headless: it renders and answers the tools, and nothing opens beside you; the footer counts it, and one click shows it. Unattended: in a goal in auto mode and its runs, where nobody is watching; elsewhere the tab is shown beside you. Always: every agent's tab. Never: every tab is shown. An agent may ask either way for one tab. |
| `browser.agents.scripts` | `allow` (Allow) \| `refuse` (Refuse) | `"allow"` | P W | **Agents may run scripts in a page** — Whether an agent may evaluate a script in a tab through browser_eval — the way a person opens the console — to read a page's state while testing it. Allow: any agent the browser tools answer. Refuse: the tool names this setting and the agent reads the page with browser_read, browser_snapshot and browser_console instead. |
| `browser.screenshot.width` | integer 320–4096 | `1280` | W M | **Screenshot width** — The width in pixels of a screenshot of a tab — the one an agent asks for with browser_screenshot, and the camera's copy. The page is scaled to it; the height follows the tab. |

## `events.*`

| Key | Kind | Default | Scopes | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `events.enabled` | bool | `true` | M | **Events are heard on this machine** — The listeners' runtime here — the ticker that looks for due schedules, checks, polls and project changes, the worker that starts runs from queued occurrences, and the hook doors. Off, nothing starts and nothing is claimed; every workflow that is On, every listening goal and their queue stay exactly as they are until this is on again. A run's own waits and boundary events go on either way. |
| `events.tick_secs` | integer 5–3600 | `15` | M | **Tick** — How often, in seconds, the runtime looks for a schedule, a check, a poll or a project change that has come due. A shorter tick notices sooner and asks the machine more often. |
| `events.check_timeout_secs` | integer 5–3600 | `60` | M | **Check timeout** — How long, in seconds, a check start's command may run. A command that hangs is the alert: past this it is terminated and counts as failing. |
| `events.files.max_depth` | integer 1–64 | `8` | M | **Files scan depth** — How many folder levels a project's files change walks when the project is a plain folder. A git project reads its own status instead; a scan that stops at the bound says so. |
| `events.files.max_entries` | integer 100–100000 | `5000` | M | **Files scan entries** — How many entries a plain folder's files scan examines before it stops. The scan reports what it saw — a partial answer on time beats a complete one that never returns. |
| `events.public_hooks` | bool | `false` | M | **Public hooks** — Whether a start event marked public may be called from outside this machine, with its secret. Off, every public hook answers as if it did not exist, and a local call under the node's token still works. The node itself binds loopback unless it is started to allow remote callers. |
| `events.pr_poll_secs` | integer 60–86400 | `300` | M | **Pull request poll** — How often, in seconds, a pull request's state is asked of its code host while a project start or a wait wants its changes. The code host rate-limits; a review is rarely faster than a few minutes. |
| `events.chain_depth` | integer 1–10 | `3` | W | **Chain depth** — How many listeners one causal line of events may pass through — a run finished, a signal raised, a review started. Enough for the compositions people build, and short enough that a mistake is visible within one tick rather than after a night of runs. |
| `events.fires_per_minute` | integer 1–600 | `30` | W | **Start rate** — How many runs one start event may begin per minute — every start but a schedule's, a person's and a hook's, which pace themselves. The backstop for causality the chain cannot see: a runaway is, by definition, fast. |
| `events.backlog_per_listener` | integer 1–100 | `5` | W | **Backlog per start** — How many occurrences may wait behind the runs a start already began. Past this an occurrence is refused, and the workflow's or the goal's row says so. |

| `mobile_development.android.sdk` | string | `""` | M | **Android SDK** — The Android SDK folder on this machine, when neither ANDROID_HOME nor ANDROID_SDK_ROOT names it and it is not in Android Studio's folder. Empty, those are read. |

| `git.fetch_interval_secs` | integer 0–3600 | `300` | W | **Fetch interval** — 0 turns it off. While an agent reviews or fixes for you, the lifecycle reads every 15 s regardless. |

| `workstreams.script.timeout_secs` | integer 1–3600 | `300` | P W | **Script timeout** — How long a workstream script may run before it is terminated and counted as failed. |

Written by Approve under About › Settings › Workstream scripts, never by hand: a project's scripts sync, and a script nobody here approved never runs here. |
| `workstreams.board.enabled` | bool | `true` | W M | **The Board** — Every workstream as a card in five columns — Backlog, Todo, Doing, Done, Archived — reached from the Project IDE's header. Off hides the Board and its doors; nothing about the workstreams changes. |
| `workstreams.board.due_soon_days` | integer 1–30 | `3` | W M | **Due soon within** — How many days before its due date a card starts reading as due soon. |
| `workstreams.board.wip_limit` | integer 0–50 | `0` | W M | **Doing limit** — How many cards the Doing column holds before its header warns. Zero is no limit. A warning, never a refusal. |

## `security.*`

| Key | Kind | Default | Scopes | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `security.redactor.enabled` | bool | `true` | W M | **Redact secrets before agents see them** — Keys, tokens and values the rules recognise are replaced by placeholders in everything the platform hands an agent or a harness, and restored only where a command is about to run on this machine. |
| `security.redactor.rules` | object or array | `[]` | W M | **Your redaction rules** — Rules of your own — a regular expression, or the name of an environment variable whose value must never reach an agent. Workspace rules and this machine's rules both apply, in that order. |
| `security.redactor.builtins_off` | object or array | `[]` | W M | **Built-in redaction rules switched off** — The ids of the shipped redaction rules that should not apply. A built-in can be switched off; it cannot be deleted. |
| `security.redactor.env_auto` | bool | `true` | M | **Recognise this node's own environment** — Every environment variable of the node process whose name says token, secret, password, key or credential is a detector: its value is redacted wherever it appears, like a rule you wrote by name. The status carries the count and the names, never a value; a name can be switched off in the built-ins list. |
| `security.guard.enabled` | bool | `true` | W M | **Guard tool calls** — Every command, path and tool an agent asks its harness to run is judged against the rules before it runs: allowed, refused with the reason, sent to you in the Inbox, or read by the classifier first. |
| `security.guard.rules` | object or array | `[]` | W M | **Your guard rules** — Rules of your own, tried in order after the built-ins: a command pattern, a path glob or a tool name — as the harness calls it, or its harness-neutral name, fetch for WebFetch — what to do when it matches, and where it applies: everywhere, the platform's agents only, or harnesses opened in a terminal only. Workspace rules come before this machine's. |
| `security.guard.builtins_off` | object or array | `[]` | W M | **Built-in guard rules switched off** — The ids of the shipped guard rules that should not apply. |
| `security.guard.terminal_hooks` | bool | `true` | M | **Guard harnesses opened in a terminal** — A Claude Code or GitHub Copilot CLI session opened in the IDE's terminal asks the node before each tool runs. When the node does not answer in time, the harness's own prompt stands — you are at the keyboard. The rules that steer an agent to the platform's own tools — the embedded browser's — leave a terminal harness be: nothing of the platform's is injected into it, so it keeps the machine's browser and its own prompt. |
| `security.classifier.enabled` | bool | `true` | W M | **Ask a model about unsure commands** — A rule with the *classify* action puts the redacted command to an agent for one line — safe, or harmful and why. No verdict, or a harmful one, goes to you; the classifier never allows what the rules did not. |
| `security.classifier.agent` | string | `"general-agent"` | W M | **Classifier agent** — The agent whose harness and models read the command. Any enabled agent; its session has no tools and no door to the platform. |
| `security.classifier.deadline_secs` | integer 5–120 | `20` | W M | **Classifier deadline (seconds)** — How long a verdict may take, launch included. Past it the call is treated as no verdict and the command goes to you. |
| `security.classifier.on_harmful` | `ask` (Ask) \| `deny` (Deny) | `"ask"` | W M | **When the classifier says harmful** — `ask` puts the call in your Inbox with the classifier's reason; `deny` refuses it outright and the agent hears why. |
| `security.classifier.provider` | `agent` (Agent) \| `harness` (Harness) \| `decision_making_agent` (Decision-Making Agent) | `"agent"` | W M | **Who reads the command** — `agent`: the classifier agent below, on its own harness and models. `harness`: one harness and one of its models, named below, with no agent in between. `decision_making_agent`: the Decision-Making Agent (Settings › Decision Settings › Decision Making), asked whether the call is harmful and in which way. Whichever reads it, no verdict or a harmful one goes to you; nothing here ever allows what the rules did not. |
| `security.classifier.harness` | string | `"claude-code"` | W M | **Classifier harness** — The harness that reads the command when the provider is `harness`. Its session has no tools and no door to the platform. |
| `security.classifier.model` | string | `"claude-sonnet-5-5[1m]"` | W M | **Classifier model** — The model of that harness that reads the command. Empty is the harness's own default. |
| `security.classifier.effort` | `minimal` (Minimal) \| `low` (Low) \| `medium` (Medium) \| `high` (High) \| `xhigh` (Extra high) \| `max` (Max) | `"high"` | W M | **Classifier effort** — How hard that model works on a verdict, when the provider is `harness`. A level the model does not take becomes the nearest one below it, and a harness with no effort control is sent none. |
| `security.content.screen` | bool | `true` | W M | **Read web content before an agent may** — A page an agent opens with the platform's browser, and a review or comment it reads from a code host, is put to the classifier first — one line: safe, or harmful and why. Harmful, or no verdict, holds the content: you see the source and the reason in the conversation (or your Inbox, in a goal), the agent reads a sentence, and Allow lets it through. Off, content is framed as data and read at once. |
| `security.content.on_harmful` | `ask` (Ask) \| `deny` (Deny) | `"ask"` | W M | **When content reads as harmful** — `ask` shows you the source, the reason and an excerpt where the agent works — Allow once, Allow this site for this conversation, or Deny; `deny` withholds it outright and the agent hears why. |
| `security.net.deny_hosts` | object or array | `[]` | W M | **Hosts a connector may never reach** — A list of hosts — `host[:port]` or `*.suffix` — the platform's own outbound calls refuse whatever a connector declares. Deny wins over every allow. Workspace and machine lists both apply. |
| `security.net.allow_hosts` | object or array | `[]` | W M | **Hosts a connector may reach beyond its own** — A list of hosts — `host[:port]` or `*.suffix` — allowed on top of the ones each connector declares. A connector's declared hosts are allowed by default; anything else is refused unless it is here. |
| `security.collaboration.classify` | bool | `true` | W M | **Read outside messages before an agent may** — A message from a person on another node is put to the classifier — one line: safe, or harmful and why — before it may wake an agent. Harmful, or no verdict, holds the message: you see it with the reason, no agent does, and Release lets it through. Off, a message from outside wakes agents like your own. |
| `security.collaboration.agent_tools` | `ask` (Ask) \| `as_owner` (As the owner) | `"ask"` | W M | **Tools on behalf of an outsider** — `ask`: an agent woken by a person on another node has every tool beyond reading put to you first, whatever the guard rules allow, and a classify verdict reads as ask. `as_owner`: the same rules as for your own messages. |
| `security.mcp.observed` | `refuse` (Refuse) \| `allow` (Allow) | `"refuse"` | W M | **Installed MCP servers on an observed harness** — Whether an MCP server installed on an agent is mounted on a harness the guard cannot judge — Codex, pi, OMP, OpenCode, a custom harness. `refuse`: the server is left off that harness and the session is told; the platform's own server is always mounted, and a judged harness (Claude Code, GitHub Copilot CLI, Grok Build, Gemini CLI, ACP) always gets every server, its tools judged like commands. `allow`: every server is mounted everywhere, and an observed harness runs its tools under its own approval prompt. |

## `decisions.*`

| Key | Kind | Default | Scopes | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `decisions.enabled` | bool | `false` | P W M | **Let the Decision-Making Agent decide** — Off, every decision point runs its own rule: a work item goes to a member of its pool by lot, an unaddressed message wakes the default agent, an auto goal adopts its workflow alone. On, the Decision-Making Agent is asked first and the rule runs when it is not sure or does not answer. An agent or a workflow can switch it on for itself alone, and an `auto_route` model plan, an effort of `auto`, a `judge` step and a classifier set to `decision_making_agent` ask it whatever this says. |
| `decisions.points_off` | object or array | `[]` | P W M | **Decision points left to their rule** — The decision points the switch above does not reach, by id: `assign.pick`, `dispatch.triage`, `goal.adopt`, `browser.headless`, `agent.decide`. A point somebody selected by name — `model.route`, `model.effort`, `security.tool`, `security.message`, `security.content`, `workflow.judge` — is not switched off here; unselect it where it was selected. |
| `decisions.provider` | `harness` (Harness) \| `agent` (Agent) \| `jev` (Jev) \| `rlcd` (Another calibrated model (RLCD)) | `"harness"` | W M | **Who decides** — `harness`: a harness on this node with one of its models. `agent`: an agent, on its own harness and models. `jev`: TypeSafe AI's Jev, a model trained for calibrated decisions, over its API. `rlcd`: any other model that speaks the same wire at an endpoint you name. Every provider is held to one answer shape; a generative model's probabilities are its own estimate, a calibrated model's mean how often it is right. |
| `decisions.harness.id` | string | `"claude-code"` | W M | **Decision harness** — The harness asked when the provider is `harness`. Its session has no tools and no door to the platform. |
| `decisions.harness.model` | string | `"claude-sonnet-5-5[1m]"` | W M | **Decision model** — The model of that harness. Empty is the harness's own default. |
| `decisions.harness.effort` | `minimal` (Minimal) \| `low` (Low) \| `medium` (Medium) \| `high` (High) \| `xhigh` (Extra high) \| `max` (Max) | `"high"` | W M | **Decision effort** — How hard that model works on a judgement, when the provider is `harness`. A level the model does not take becomes the nearest one below it, and a harness with no effort control is sent none. |
| `decisions.agent.id` | string | `"general-agent"` | W M | **Decision agent** — The agent asked when the provider is `agent`. Any enabled agent; it answers with no tools. |
| `decisions.jev.model` | string | `"jev-latest"` | W M | **Jev model** — The Jev model asked when the provider is `jev`. The API key is kept in this machine's keystore, never here. |
| `decisions.rlcd.endpoint` | string | `""` | W M | **Endpoint** — The base URL asked when the provider is `rlcd` — the platform posts to `/v1/systemone` under it. Its host passes the outbound host lists like any other. |
| `decisions.rlcd.model` | string | `""` | W M | **Endpoint model** — The model named in each request to that endpoint. |
| `decisions.rlcd.auth` | `none` (None) \| `bearer` (Bearer token) | `"bearer"` | W M | **Endpoint sign-in** — `bearer` sends the key kept in this machine's keystore as a bearer token; `none` sends nothing, for a model served on this machine. |
| `decisions.deadline_secs` | integer 5–120 | `20` | W M | **Decision deadline (seconds)** — How long one judgement may take, retries included. Past it the decision point runs its own rule; a security point asks you. |
| `decisions.retries` | integer 0–5 | `2` | W M | **Decision retries** — How many times a judgement is asked again after a transient failure — a rate limit, an overloaded or unreachable provider, an answer that does not hold to the shape. A refused key or a refused request is never retried. |
| `decisions.confidence.act` | number 0–1 | `0.7` | P W M | **Confidence to act on** — How sure a judgement must be for a decision point to take it. Below it the point runs its own rule, and the judgement is recorded as unsure. |
| `decisions.confidence.security` | number 0.5–1 | `0.9` | W M | **Confidence to call a command safe** — How sure the Decision-Making Agent must be that a call is not harmful for the classifier to read it as safe. Anything less is no verdict, and the call goes to you. |

## `agents.*`

| Key | Kind | Default | Scopes | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `agents.default` | string | `"general-agent"` | P W | **Default agent** — The agent an unaddressed message reaches — in a project's threads when set there. |
| `agents.effort` | `auto` (Auto) \| `minimal` (Minimal) \| `low` (Low) \| `medium` (Medium) \| `high` (High) \| `xhigh` (Extra high) \| `max` (Max) | `"high"` | P W | **Effort** — How hard a model works on a task when nobody said otherwise — a workflow step's own effort comes first, then the model's, then the agent's. `auto`: the Decision-Making Agent reads the task and names the level; when it is off, unsure or does not answer, the level is `high`. A level the model does not take becomes the nearest one below it, and a harness with no effort control is sent none. |
| `agents.conversation.mode` | `manual` (Manual) \| `auto` (Auto) \| `plan` (Plan) | `"manual"` | P W M | **New IDE conversations start in** — How far an agent goes on its own in a conversation about a project or a workstream; the composer changes it per conversation at any time. `manual`: edits land and wait for your Keep or Undo, and a command no guard rule decided is asked in the conversation. `auto`: edits land and commands run under the guard and the classifier; the changes stay reviewable and are kept when you send your next message. `plan`: the agent reads and replies with a plan — an edit is refused, a command is asked — and *Build this plan* hands it over. The guard's rules, the Redactor and the classifier hold in every mode. |
| `agents.review.checkpoints` | integer 1–200 | `20` | W M | **Turns kept restorable** — How many turns of a conversation keep what they changed, so *Restore to before this message* can go back. A turn with a change still waiting for your word is never dropped. |
| `agents.context.selection_max_lines` | integer 20–2000 | `400` | W | **Selection chip max lines** |
| `agents.context.terminal_lines` | integer 20–2000 | `200` | W | **Terminal chip lines** |

## `goals.*`

| Key | Kind | Default | Scopes | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `goals.default_mode` | `auto` (Auto) \| `guided` (Guided) \| `manual` (Manual) | `"auto"` | W M | **New goals start in** — The mode a goal is captured in when the capture does not say. `auto`: the Workflow Agent designs the workflow and the platform adopts it, starts the run, repairs and restarts it by itself; a step that may write runs commands too (`goals.auto.ceiling`), a permission above a step's ceiling is read by the classifier (`goals.auto.permissions`), and only a step a person must take, a guard rule that asks or refuses, a call the classifier finds harmful, a gated publish or a question the agent still asks wait for you. `guided`: the agent proposes and you adopt, ask for changes or decline. `manual`: you design on the goal's Workflow tab, with the agent on request. |
| `goals.auto.repair_limit` | integer 0–20 | `3` | W M | **Auto repairs before asking** — How many failed runs an auto goal repairs and restarts on its own. Past the limit the Workflow Agent's corrected proposal waits for your decision, so a goal that keeps failing cannot loop unattended. |
| `goals.auto.permissions` | `classify` (Classify) \| `ask` (Ask) | `"classify"` | W M | **Above a step's ceiling in an auto goal** — What happens in an auto goal when an agent wants a tool above its step's ceiling — the ceiling `goals.auto.ceiling` sets — and no guard rule decides it. `classify`: the classifier reads the redacted call — safe runs, harmful asks you or is refused as `security.classifier.on_harmful` says, no verdict asks you. `ask`: the call is put to you, as in a guided goal. The guard's rules and the redactor come first either way; a guided or manual goal always asks. |
| `goals.auto.ceiling` | `exec` (Runs commands) \| `step` (The step's own) | `"exec"` | W M | **A step's ceiling in an auto goal** — The ceiling a step's session runs under in an auto goal, where nobody is watching. `exec`: a step that may change files may also run commands and the MCP tools that act — an ordinary command runs on its own, the guard's rules and the redactor first as ever, and a read-only step stays read-only. `step`: every step keeps the ceiling its design gives it, and what is above it is `goals.auto.permissions`'s to settle — the earlier behaviour. A guided or manual goal keeps its step's ceiling either way. |

| `cache.git_status.ttl_ms` | integer 0–600000 | `2000` | M | **Git status cache** — How long a workstream's git status is reused before running git again. |
| `cache.path_index.ttl_ms` | integer 0–600000 | `5000` | M | **Path-index cache** — How long a root's file-path index is reused before walking the tree again. |

| `cache.model_health.ttl_ms` | integer 0–60000 | `500` | M | **Model-health snapshot cache** — How long the model-health snapshot is reused before rebuilding it. |
| `cache.harness_usage.ttl_ms` | integer 0–3600000 | `180000` | M | **Harness usage cache** — How long a harness account's usage report is reused before its source is asked again — a provider's usage endpoint is not a thing to hit on every render. |

| `cache.desktop.network_poll_ms` | integer 5000–3600000 | `30000` | M | **Network poll** — How often the desktop footer reads this Mac's network — the VPN, the route, the resolvers, System Settings' proxy — and what the platform's calls leave through, while a window is visible. |

| Key | Kind | Default | Scopes | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `network.proxy.mode` | `environment` (The environment's) \| `none` (None) \| `manual` (Manual) | `"environment"` | M | **Proxy** — `environment`: the proxy the node's own environment names (`HTTPS_PROXY`, `HTTP_PROXY`, `NO_PROXY`), if any — what a terminal-started node inherits; the desktop-started node inherits none. `none`: no proxy, whatever the environment says — and nothing the platform runs is handed one. `manual`: the two URLs and the bypass list below, for the platform's own calls and everything it runs. |
| `network.proxy.http` | string | `""` | M | **HTTP proxy** — A URL: `http://proxy.example:3128`, with a login as `http://user:password@…` when the proxy asks for one. Empty means none for `http://` targets. |

| `network.http1_only` | bool | `false` | M | **Speak HTTP/1.1 only** — Every request the platform makes uses HTTP/1.1, never HTTP/2 — for a proxy or an inspection tool that does not speak it. Git the platform runs follows (`http.version`); a harness's own calls are its own. |
| `network.public_ip_url` | string | `"https://api.ipify.org"` | M | **Public IP service** — The service asked for this machine's public address — one `https://` URL that answers the address as plain text, such as `https://api.ipify.org`. The desktop app reads it for the footer's network word and Settings › Capabilities › Network; the node never does. Empty turns the read off, and the internet is then judged by a TCP connect alone. |

## `sync.*`

| Key | Kind | Default | Scopes | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sync.enabled` | bool | `false` | M | **Sync over relays** — Whether this node talks to relays at all. Off by default: nothing is contacted until you turn it on. Off, no invite can be claimed, no hosted member hears anything, and nothing you joined moves — the workspace works alone. |
| `sync.relays` | object or array | `["wss://relay.nostr.com","wss://relay.nostr.net","wss://relay.damus.io","wss://nos.lol"]` | M | **Relays** — The Nostr relays this node publishes to and reads from, as `wss://` (or `ws://` on this machine) URLs. Four public relays are the defaults — relay.nostr.com, relay.nostr.net, relay.damus.io, nos.lol — and any may be replaced; they see ciphertext addressed to pubkeys and nothing else. An entry that is not a `ws://` or `wss://` URL is refused when written, naming it. A change is picked up at once — no restart. |
| `sync.interval_secs` | integer 5–3600 | `30` | M | **Catch-up every (seconds)** — How often the node asks the relays for what it missed while a live subscription was down. |
| `sync.publish_relay_list` | bool | `true` | M | **Publish the relay list** — Publish a NIP-65 relay list under this node's pubkey — the hint an invite carries, and what lets a person who lost the link find this node again. Plaintext: the relay URLs and nothing else. |
| `sync.iroh.enabled` | bool | `true` | M | **Direct connections** — Open a direct QUIC endpoint for attachment bytes between this node and the people it hosts or is hosted by. Local-only by default: no outside infrastructure is contacted unless the next switch says so. |
| `sync.iroh.n0_relays` | bool | `false` | M | **Use n0's public relays for direct connections** — Let the direct endpoint use n0's public relay servers to reach a node behind a NAT. Off, only addresses you or a peer announced are tried. On contacts infrastructure operated by n0. |
| `sync.iroh.peers` | object or array | `[]` | M | **Direct peers by hand** — Peers reached without any relay, for a LAN: a list of `{member_pubkey, node_id, addrs}`. Empty means peers are learned from their announcements. |
